text:
We will explore some null spaces in this activity and see why $\nul(A)$ satisfies the definition of a subspace.

Consider the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp 3 \amp -1 \amp 2 \\ -2 \amp 0 \amp -4 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp 1 \end{bmatrix} $$ and give a parametric description of the solution space to the equation $A\xvec = \zerovec$. In other words, give a parametric description of $\nul(A)$.

This parametric description shows that the vectors satisfying the equation $A\xvec=\zerovec$ can be written as a linear combination of a set of vectors. In other words, this description shows why $\nul(A)$ is the span of a set of vectors and is therefore a subspace. Identify a set of vectors whose span is $\nul(A)$.

Use this set of vectors to find a basis for $\nul(A)$ and state the dimension of $\nul(A)$.

The null space $\nul(A)$ is a subspace of $\real^p$ for which value of $p$?

Now consider the matrix $B$ whose reduced row echelon form is given by $$ B \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp -3 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$ Give a parametric description of $\nul(B)$.

The parametric description gives a set of vectors that span $\nul(B)$. Explain why this set of vectors is linearly independent and hence forms a basis. What is the dimension of $\nul(B)$?

For a general matrix $A$, how does the number of pivot positions indicate the dimension of $\nul(A)$?

Suppose that the columns of a matrix $A$ are linearly independent. What can you say about $\nul(A)$?
